findings.location: Admonition box 'do external controls reproduce concurrent ones?' (subsection 'Adoption, acceptance, and the gap that remains')
findings.claim_text: the burden of covariate adjustment for the latter is heavy — one external-control effort screened more than 120 potential confounders {cite:p}`Swaminathan2023, Walker2024, Struebing2024`
findings.issue: Quantitative-attribution mismatch. The specific figure 'more than 120 potential confounders' is attached to Swaminathan2023, Walker2024 and Struebing2024, but none of these three carries a >120-confounder source sentence in the evidence package. The only verbatim '>120 potential confounding variables' in the package belongs to Yap2022 (the CAROLINA-study RWD external-control replication), which the section cites correctly elsewhere ('sometimes more than a hundred covariates {cite:p}`...Yap2022...`').
findings.evidence: Yap2022 effect_size_source_sentence: 'the authors ... using propensity score matching to control for >120 potential confounding variables.' Swaminathan2023/Walker2024/Struebing2024 findings report treatment-effect comparability and hazard ratios, not a confounder count.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Yap2022 to (or substitute it into) the citation group for the '>120 potential confounders' clause, or soften to 'heavy covariate adjustment' without the specific 120 figure for those three papers. e.g. '...the burden of covariate adjustment for the latter is heavy, with one real-world external-control effort screening more than 120 potential confounders {cite:p}`Yap2022`.'

findings.claim_text: 9 of the 22 packaged conflicts are not represented in the section.
findings.issue: All 9 unrepresented conflicts concern general FAIR data-sharing (mandate compliance, ontology annotation, proteomics 'data tombs', OMOP semantic adequacy, open-data citation advantage, willingness-to-share incentives). They are out of scope for this VCG/control-data-reuse section, which explicitly defers the FAIR-failure topic to sec-fair-preclinical. 8 of the 9 even reference papers absent from this section's findings[]. All 13 in-scope VCG/control-data/Bayesian-borrowing conflicts (package indices 9-21) ARE represented with both sides. No fix required; documented for accounting transparency.
findings.evidence: In-scope conflict survival = 13/13 = 100%. Overall = 13/22 = 59% (> 0.50 threshold). Suppressed set is entirely cluster_04.
findings.suggested_fix: None. Curator over-inclusion from a merged cluster_04+cluster_05 package; the section correctly scopes itself to control-data reuse.

findings.location: Subsection 'How faithfully do virtual controls reproduce real ones?'
findings.claim_text: Re-analysing twenty sub-chronic non-human-primate studies with the concurrent control omitted, 82% of statistically significant parameter differences were confirmed ... {cite:p}`Mecklenburg2023`
findings.issue: Minor scope imprecision: the package describes Mecklenburg2023's 20 studies as '(sub)chronic' (a mix of subchronic and chronic NHP studies); the prose labels all twenty 'sub-chronic'. The 82% (18/22 parameters) and 'all four dose-limiting toxicities' values are exact.
findings.evidence: study_system: '20 (sub)chronic NHP toxicity studies'. Source: 'out of 22 parameters with statistical difference ... 82% could be confirmed using the mixed-design ANOVA.'
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'twenty sub-chronic non-human-primate studies' to 'twenty subchronic and chronic non-human-primate studies'.

findings.location: Subsection 'Why the dividend is conditional: drift and comparability' (strain-dependence sentence)
findings.claim_text: ...body-weight and diet control alone shift terminal background liver-tumour incidence into a 15–20% band {cite:p}`Leakey2003`.
findings.issue: The sentence frames a list as 'strain-dependent' background variability drawn mostly from rat data (Leydig-cell/MNCL/pituitary in rats), but the Leakey2003 15-20% liver-tumour figure is from B6C3F1 mice (and Boyle2018 from Tg.rasH2 mice). Mixing rat and mouse strains under one 'strain-dependent' umbrella is defensible (both rodents) but the species shift is unflagged.
findings.evidence: Leakey2003 study_system: 'B6C3F1 mouse chronic bioassay background liver tumor incidence'; source predicts 'terminal background liver tumor incidence of 15-20%'.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally note the species shift, e.g. '...and, in B6C3F1 mice, body-weight and diet control alone shift terminal background liver-tumour incidence into a 15-20% band {cite:p}`Leakey2003`.'

summary.notes: All 173 cited keys resolve to the package (0 hallucinations). ~40 quantitative claims spot-checked against verbatim package source sentences (findings[] + figure_data[]); all supported.
